# KingCode Lens — llms.txt

> Web apps for Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses — previewed in your browser, no hardware needed.

KingCode Lens (v1.0.0) is a CWI software product: a simulator lab plus a
conformance-tested adapter stack for building web apps targeting the
Meta Ray-Ban Display 600x600 additive display, and an invocable on-eyewear
voice agent ("Hey KingCode") with a glanceable avatar.

## Canonical resources

- Product: https://github.com/CumulativeWebInc/cwi-kingcode-lens
- Live simulator: https://cumulativewebinc.github.io/cwi-kingcode-lens/
- Release: https://github.com/CumulativeWebInc/cwi-kingcode-lens/releases/tag/v1.0.0
- Docs: quickstart.md, simulator-lab.md, qa-checklist.md, licensing.md
- Machine-readable: .well-known/agent-card.json

## Key facts (verified 2026-09-18)

- Simulator only. No tests have run on physical eyewear. No on-hardware claims.
- Meta's Ray-Ban Display web-app path exposes no camera, microphone, or
  notifications (Meta's official docs, verbatim). The meta-display backend
  is display-first; voice is handled via the phone companion.
- D-pad input: Neural Band / captouch translate to arrow-key + Enter events.
- Additive display: black is transparent; app backgrounds must be near-black.
- 117/117 tests green (node --test). Zero dependencies.

## Honest limits

- No Meta partnership, endorsement, or review — ever.
- STT/TTS/wake-word are simulation points with documented production seams.
- Android XR backend is a declared stub (connect() throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED).
- Invention notes are defensive disclosure, not a patent.
